:::{#def-interval}
#### Interval

For [real numbers](notation.qmd#def-real-numbers) $a \le b$,
the **intervals** with **endpoints** $a$ and $b$ are:

- the **closed interval** $[a, b] \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a \le x \le b}$;
- the **open interval** $(a, b) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a < x < b}$;
- the **half-open intervals** $[a, b) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a \le x < b}$
  and $(a, b] \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : a < x \le b}$.

The **unbounded intervals** have at most one endpoint:

- $[a, \infty) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x \ge a}$
  and $(a, \infty) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x > a}$;
- $(-\infty, b] \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x \le b}$
  and $(-\infty, b) \eqdef \set{x \in \reals : x < b}$;
- $(-\infty, \infty) \eqdef \reals$.

A square bracket means the endpoint belongs to the interval,
and a parenthesis means it does not.
The symbols $\infty$ and $-\infty$ are not real numbers,
so they always get a parenthesis.

:::
